chunks: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

Whoever visits a Muslim person during his illness, on that day seventy thousand angels send blessings upon him — if it was in the morning, until the evening, and if it was in the evening, until the morning — along with that, for him is a corner in Paradise.

key_terms.خَرِيفٌ فِي الْجَنَّةِ: a corner/garden in Paradise — a specific portion or dwelling in the afterlife
key_terms.صَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: sent blessings upon him — divine/angelic invocation of mercy
key_terms.عَادَ: visited (the sick) — 'iyada, the Islamic practice of visiting ill persons

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting a sick Muslim according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches that visiting a sick Muslim carries immense spiritual reward: seventy thousand angels continuously send blessings upon the visitor for the entire day or night. This hadith is found in al-Kafi's chapter on the rewards of visiting the sick, emphasizing that acts of social solidarity, particularly caring for the ill, are elevated as acts of worship equivalent in spiritual gravity to angelic intercession.
